sections.name: General
sections.description: Orientation pieces for understanding Upgrade Society and the transition it explores.

items.title: What Could an Upgraded Society Look Like?
items.description: A concise overview of why the old model feels fragile and how more affordable, resilient and cooperative ways of living could emerge.

sections.name: Co-Created Money
sections.description: Money creation, universal dividends, Ğ1 and experiments in human-centered monetary systems.

items.title: History of Money
items.description: A historical introduction to the recurring idea that communities can create exchange media themselves through mutual credit and related systems.

items.title: What is Co-Created Money
items.description: The clearest conceptual introduction: instead of redistributing money after creation, participants share equally in creating it from the beginning.

items.title: The Universal Dividend — How Money Is Created
items.description: A focused explanation of Ğ1’s Universal Dividend: every human participant creates money equally through time.

items.title: Ğ1 (June) — Introduction to Ğ1
items.description: A practical introduction to Ğ1, the Relative Theory of Money and human-based issuance compared with fiat and Bitcoin.

items.title: The Libre Money Experiment, Ğ1 and the Economics of Universal Dividend
items.description: A compact technical outline of Ğ1, the Universal Dividend, monetary symmetry and the Relative Theory of Money.

items.title: The Libre Currency: Ğ1 and the Future of Human-Centered Money
items.description: The deepest existing guide to Ğ1, covering its monetary theory, implementation, Web of Trust and broader philosophy.

items.title: G1 — The Currency of Trust
items.description: A moral and institutional argument for Ğ1 as money built around trust rather than debt-based dependence.

sections.name: The World Now
sections.description: Diagnosis of the pressures shaping everyday life: money, work, generational change, conflict and institutional strain.

items.title: Why the Fiat System Is Useless for the Working Class
items.description: An argument that financialized fiat money has broken the connection between work, saving and long-term security for ordinary earners.

items.title: The Problem Is Simpler Than We Think
items.description: A structural diagnosis that traces housing, wages and credit problems back to how new money is created and who gets first access to it.

items.title: Why the Millennials Will Lead the New Change
items.description: A generational argument that people promised stability but given debt, inflation and insecurity may become the builders of new institutions.

items.title: Why Is There So Much Conflict and Trauma in the World?
items.description: A structural exploration of conflict, resentment and burnout through powerlessness, monetary systems and institutional design.

sections.name: Nation States
sections.description: How nation-states, public finance and large-scale political order may change through the coming transition.

items.title: From 2025 to 2050 — The World in Transition
items.description: A future scenario in which nation-states remain but everyday life becomes more local, regional and networked as centralized legitimacy weakens.

items.title: BitBonds
items.description: A speculative proposal for euro-denominated bonds collateralized by Bitcoin as a bridge between hard digital collateral and public finance.

sections.name: Cooperatives
sections.description: Cooperatives, upgraded communities, hubs and local economic institutions that can be built in practice.

items.title: What Are Upgraded Communities?
items.description: A place-first vision of affordable, calmer and more resilient communities that reduce dependence on distant systems without requiring national revolution.

items.title: The Cooperative Century
items.description: A multi-decade roadmap from small cooperatives and experimental currencies toward a mature civic and cooperative economy.

items.title: Upgrade Hubs
items.description: A practical concept for temporary co-living gatherings in depopulating regions to test community, regenerative living and alternative economies.

items.title: The Ğ1 Society & Regional Depopulation
items.description: An applied strategy combining Ğ1 with depopulated regions to explore lower-cost, higher-autonomy community life today.

sections.name: Beyond Left and Right
sections.description: Political and economic ideas that do not fit neatly inside the inherited socialism-versus-capitalism divide.

items.title: The Third Way — Between Socialism and Capitalism
items.description: A proposed synthesis beyond the twentieth-century capitalism/socialism divide using co-created money, localism, cooperation and decentralization.

sections.name: About
sections.description: About Upgrade Society, authorship and editorial provenance.
